statements.text: A genuine crash of the primary implementation process is different: first attempt safe recovery, including restoring the existing session or reconstructing context when possible. If primary execution remains unrecoverable **before a PR has been published**, move the card to `Failed`, even when partial code changes exist. Preserve changes and diagnostics; do not automatically publish interrupted implementation work as a draft PR. **After a PR has been published**, an unrecoverable primary session or correction operation is an operation failure, not a terminal task failure: preserve the existing PR, unshipped work, and project ownership; report the blockage, make bounded safe recovery attempts, and remain in an explicit recoverable waiting state or await a human merge/closure. Never move an open-PR card to `Failed` or claim a new task simply because post-publication automation failed. A temporary external outage follows the separate preservation-and-retry policy.

statements.text: Use the existing bounded operation retry configuration for primary implementation crash recovery; do not add a separate implementation-crash retry setting. statements.text: Only one orchestrator instance may actively own and process a given project at a time, including when another instance is running locally or in Docker on the same machine. statements.text: Validate the complete refinement result before changing the Trello card. Persist the original values and intended complete update before the first external write. If refinement cannot complete, reconcile or restore the original title, description, and classification rather than leaving a partial final result; move the card to `Failed` with an explanation only after that outcome is verified. If Trello is unavailable or an earlier write has an uncertain outcome, retain ownership and a pending recovery state until it can be safely reconciled; never report successful refinement or confirmed restoration without verification. Before refinement writes, including completion or rollback, compare current fields with the saved originals and verified orchestrator writes, and do not knowingly overwrite detected human changes. After writes, verify the resulting fields and inspect available change history for concurrent edits, including edits accepted between the final read and the write. Preserve recoverable human content and evidence; on conflicting or unattributable changes, pause further writes with retained project ownership and explicitly reconcile or request operator resolution before declaring completion or restoration. These checks detect and reconcile conflicts conservatively; without a supported conditional-write or serialization mechanism, they do not provide atomic compare-and-write behavior or guarantee that every concurrent overwrite can be prevented.

statements.text: Support an optional global limit on how many projects can actively execute AI work at once, in addition to the one-active-task-per-project rule.

statements.text: Projects waiting for available execution capacity retain their task order and state. When no global limit is configured, there is no orchestrator-imposed cross-project concurrency limit.

statements.text: Waiting for human review does not consume a global execution slot. Such a project still cannot start another task until its PR reaches a terminal outcome, but other projects may use the available execution capacity.

statements.text: When the global execution limit is reached, waiting projects receive available capacity in first-come, first-served order. A busy project must not repeatedly bypass waiting projects; configurable project priorities are not required.

statements.text: Never expose secrets in orchestrator or child-process logs, AI prompts, Trello comments, GitHub pull requests, or email notifications. Enforce least-privilege credential access, avoid forwarding configured secrets into unrelated processes or prompts, redact registered secret values and recognized encodings from outputs under orchestrator control, and treat attachments or repository content that may contain sensitive data as untrusted. Unknown or arbitrarily transformed secrets cannot be proven absent by finite scanners: verification must report which controlled channels and known-secret forms were actually checked without claiming universal detection.

unbulletedStatements.text: This document defines the intended behavior of Agent Orchestrator, not a description of the current implementation. It is the authoritative source for the verifiable specification. Changes to agreed behavior must be made explicitly and reflected in the specification.
unbulletedStatements.assessment: Applied as audit precedence; no requirement/specification edits permitted or performed.

unbulletedStatements.text: Agent Orchestrator automatically turns Trello tasks into implemented, tested, and reviewed GitHub pull requests using AI agents. It manages the end-to-end workflow while allowing humans to control the final outcome.
unbulletedStatements.assessment: Concrete lifecycle/readiness/human-control criteria supply testable parts; meaningful implementation/model semantics remain qualified, not universal quality guarantee.

unbulletedStatements.text: The highest-priority goal of every implementation task is to produce a GitHub pull request.
unbulletedStatements.assessment: Read with explicitly agreed primary-crash/no-meaningful-change/safety exceptions; not unconditional publication of interrupted or artificial work.
